#+TITLE: Fixtures Designed But Not Built
#+AUTHOR: Daniel Okuniewicz Jr.
#+DATE: 2026-08-23

* Designed 2026-08-23 and 2026-08-25; the built ones say so in their heading

Each entry below is a fixture this tree *needs* and does not have, with what it
pins and how to build it. They came out of reading the GeoPackage Encoding
Standard's normative SQL (OGC 12-128r19, Annex C and the extension annexes)
against what this crate writes -- see =handoff.org= § BUGS FOUND entries 16--18
and =plans/same-format-fidelity.org= § THE DEFECTS, defect 6.

*Read =HOSTILE.org= first* for the naming rules and the standing requirement
that every fixture be *confirmed readable by geosetta without error* before it
is committed.

*** BUILT 2026-08-23: =spec_conformant.gpkg=
/The entry that stood at the top of this file -- "the one that matters most" --
has been built and is documented in =HOSTILE.org= under the new =spec_= prefix./
Its DDL is transcribed mechanically from the annexes at a *pinned commit*
(=fe83fdd=), by =tests/fixtures/build_spec_fixtures.sh=, which starts from an
empty file rather than from =gdal_hostile.gpkg= the way
=build_sqlite_fixtures.sh= does -- that difference is the entire point of it.

It closed the substring-assertion gap it was designed for.
=the_registry_ddl_is_what_the_standard_says= compares *whole normalised DDL*
per table, and =MasterObject= gained a =sql= field so that comparison could be
written at all. **All six registry tables this crate emits match the
standard exactly**, so the 2026-08-23 spec pass holds up under a check that
does not depend on anyone remembering what to assert.

** BUILT 2026-08-25: =sqlite_fid_gap.gpkg= extended
/Designed and built the same day, for the metadata pair. Documented in
=HOSTILE.org= with the rest of that fixture; the entry is kept here because
what it pins is a **corpus-wide** gap rather than one file's contents, and that
is the part worth not rediscovering./

*Not a new file.* The fixture already existed (built 2026-08-25 for
=handoff.org= entry 19) and needed two more rows in a table it already carried,
which is why this entry names an extension rather than a =gpkg_= stem of its
own.

***What is uncovered, and it is the same blindness that hid entry 19.***
Measured across every =.gpkg= in this tree on 2026-08-25, *every*
=gpkg_metadata_reference= row is =table=-scoped with a NULL =row_id_value=:

#+begin_src text
  gdal_hostile        table   row_id_value NULL
  gdal_linestring_z   table   row_id_value NULL
  gdal_tiles          table   row_id_value NULL   (x2)
  sqlite_altered      table   row_id_value NULL
  sqlite_constraints  table   row_id_value NULL
  sqlite_contents     table   row_id_value NULL
  sqlite_fid_gap      table   row_id_value NULL
  spec_conformant     (the pair present, zero reference rows)
#+end_src

So not one =row=, =column= or =row/col= reference exists anywhere. **The entire
class of reference that Requirement 99, decision 27 and
=container-reconciliation.org= D5 are about is untestable**, and an
implementation that silently dropped every row-scoped reference -- or carried
one pointing at a rowid that no longer exists -- would pass the whole suite and
both oracles in =tests/gpkg_oracles.rs=.

*Why this fixture and not another.* =sqlite_fid_gap.gpkg= is the only file in
the tree whose feature ids are **not** their positions (=cities= at =1, 9, 40=),
so it is the only place a row-scoped reference can point at an id that a
renumbering would move. Putting the reference anywhere else tests that a
pointer survives a rewrite that was never going to disturb it.

*Build:* extend =build_fid_fixture.sh=, after the =cities= edits, with

#+begin_src text
  INSERT INTO gpkg_metadata_reference
    (reference_scope, table_name, column_name, row_id_value, md_file_id)
    VALUES ('row', 'cities', NULL, 9, 1);
  INSERT INTO gpkg_metadata_reference
    (reference_scope, table_name, column_name, row_id_value, md_file_id)
    VALUES ('column', 'cities', 'name', NULL, 1);
#+end_src

Point the =row= scope at **9**, the middle gap id: =1= is where a renumbering
would coincidentally still be right and =40= is where it would obviously be
wrong, and 9 is the one that is wrong *without looking wrong*. The =column= row
costs nothing extra and covers the third scope; =name= is a column the write
keeps, so it exercises the *surviving* branch rather than the dropped one.

*Pins* /(all three now have tests named for them)/: that a carried =row=-scoped reference still names the feature it named,
that a =column=-scoped reference is validated against =writer::columns_for='s
output rather than replayed, and -- once =writer::feature_ids= reissues a
layer's ids because a consumer deleted from the middle -- that the reference
into that layer is dropped rather than left lying. /That last one is the guard
=container-reconciliation.org= D5 says belongs wherever a **rowid changes**, and
this is the fixture that can fail without it./

*Note on the parent file's DDL:* =sqlite_fid_gap.gpkg= inherits
=gdal_hostile.gpkg='s hand-built =gpkg_metadata_reference=, which declares
**neither** =crmr_*_fk= foreign key. That is deliberate and is what makes the
fixture sharp: =foreign_key_check= cannot see a dangling reference here, so
whatever catches it has to be this crate's own validation. Do not add the
constraints to the fixture.

** =sqlite_sequence.gpkg= -- /narrowed 2026-08-23; renamed 2026-08-24; still worth building/
/Designed as =gpkg_metadata_autoincrement.gpkg=. Renamed when =gdal_tiles.gpkg=
made the rule explicit: **these names carry provenance, not content.** What it
pins is a =sqlite_sequence= state, which is SQLite's behaviour rather than the
standard's, and the cheap build is =gdal_hostile.gpkg= plus =sqlite3=
statements -- so it is a =sqlite_*= fixture and belongs in
=build_sqlite_fixtures.sh= beside the other three./
=gpkg_metadata= is specified as =id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT=, so a
populated one *requires a =sqlite_sequence= row*.

***Two thirds of this entry was already covered and nobody had checked.***
=gdal_hostile.gpkg= and =sqlite_contents.gpkg= both carry a =gpkg_metadata=
that declares AUTOINCREMENT with a live =sqlite_sequence= row, so "a populated
=gpkg_metadata= needs a sequence row" needed no new fixture at all -- it needed
somebody to run =SELECT * FROM sqlite_sequence= against the fixtures already
here. The gap itself was closed on 2026-08-23 without this file.

*What is still uncovered, and it is the sharp part:* in every fixture in this
tree the mark **equals** =max(id)=. The state that distinguishes a high-water
mark from a recomputable maximum -- a mark *above* =max(id)=, left behind by a
deleted row -- appears nowhere. Until it does, a carrying implementation that
recomputed the mark from the rows would pass every test here.

*Build:* =sqlite3=, the Metadata extension's DDL, two rows, then delete the
second. That leaves =seq= at 2 with =max(id)= of 1.

*Build:* =sqlite3=, the Metadata extension's DDL, two rows, then delete one so
the high-water mark exceeds =max(id)= -- which is the only state that makes
the sequence row observable rather than derivable.

*** BUILT 2026-08-24: =gdal_tiles.gpkg=
/Documented in =HOSTILE.org=, and built by
=build_tile_fixture.sh= -- a script rather than a recorded command line,
because the input is a raster and the pixels have to be generated./

**It came out one thing larger than designed, and the addition was forced.**
The entry below asked for a tile pyramid; a *tiles-only* GeoPackage is
**rejected by this reader** -- =GeoPackage has no feature layers= -- against
=HOSTILE.org='s standing rule that every fixture is readable without error. So
=cities= from =gdal_hostile.gpkg= sits beside the pyramid, and that turned out
to be the useful half: the layer is EPSG:4326 and the pyramid EPSG:3857, so the
file carries an =srs_id= no feature layer accounts for, which is exactly what
=same-format-fidelity.org= M3b requirement 1 has to reconcile.

*Both of the entry's measured warnings held.* The 2048² source at
=GoogleMapsCompatible= yields 64 tiles, and a burned raster was necessary --
the all-nodata trap is real. Two facts the entry did not have: the tile table
carries **six triggers**, which are schema objects on a carried table that are
neither index nor DDL; and =gpkg_tile_matrix= has **14 rows for 2 populated
zoom levels**, so anything recomputing it from the tiles present writes a
different file.

/The entry as designed follows./

**** =gpkg_tiles.gpkg= -- as designed 2026-08-23, under the name it was designed with
A real tile pyramid: several tiles across two zoom levels, with complete
=gpkg_tile_matrix_set= and =gpkg_tile_matrix= rows.

*Pins:* D8 -- a tile pyramid is *carried*, as independent container content,
and no file is rejected for holding one. =sqlite_contents.gpkg= carries a
*minimal* one row deep, enough to pin bug 14's reporting; it is not enough to
test *carrying*, which has to move real BLOB payloads across the rewrite.

*Build:* =gdal_translate -of GPKG= over a small raster, or =sqlite3= directly
from the tiles DDL. /Prefer GDAL here/ -- unlike the registry DDL above, the
tile *data* is exactly the case where a real producer's output is what occurs.

/Measured 2026-08-23 while running =container-reconciliation.org= D2, so the
shape is known before anyone builds it:/ =gdal_translate -of GPKG -co
TILING_SCHEME=GoogleMapsCompatible= over a 2048² 3-band source yields **64
tiles**, and the table is

#+begin_src text
  CREATE TABLE "imagery" (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, zoom_level INTEGER NOT NULL,
    tile_column INTEGER NOT NULL, tile_row INTEGER NOT NULL, tile_data BLOB NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE (zoom_level, tile_column, tile_row))
#+end_src

So a tile table is the *only* mergeable table that both declares AUTOINCREMENT
and owns an index -- and its index key is three integers, needing no collation.
*Use a burned raster, not =gdal_create= alone:* an all-nodata source produced a
=gpkg= with the full DDL and **zero** tile rows, because GDAL skips blank
tiles, and a fixture built that way would exercise nothing.

** BUILT 2026-10-13: =sqlite_nullkey.gpkg= -- /renamed 2026-08-24/
/Designed as =gpkg_range_constraints.gpkg=, and renamed for the same reason as
the entry above -- with the stem changed as well as the prefix. The =range=
rows are the *vehicle*; what the fixture pins is that **a =UNIQUE= key with a
nullable member does not make a set**, which is why the entry immediately
generalises it to =ge_tce= and =gdc_tn=. Naming it after the vehicle would have
buried the finding./

/Built for =container-reconciliation.org= § 3 and documented in =HOSTILE.org=.
Two things the entry below did not have: the =enum= half had to be built
*beside* the =range= half -- without two rows whose =value= is the only
difference, the rule can be written as "drop =value= from the key" and no test
objects -- and **GDAL 3.13.3 does declare =gdcc_ntv=**, contrary to the line
below, so the reason for replacing the DDL is =gdal_hostile.gpkg='s hand-built
table rather than =ogr2ogr='s. This is also the first fixture in the tree whose
=gpkg -> gpkg= write is deliberately **refused**, which =tests/gpkg_oracles.rs=
now asserts rather than skips./

/The entry as designed follows./

*Build it on =gdal_hostile.gpkg=*, with the Schema annex's
=gpkg_data_column_constraints= DDL applied on top -- =ogr2ogr= omits the
=gdcc_ntv= constraint, so a plain GDAL base has nothing to pin. That is the
=sqlite_*= recipe exactly, and it keeps the question the fixture asks ("what
does the *format* permit?") matched to the prefix. /Building it from
=spec_conformant.gpkg= instead would be a =spec_= fixture asking a different
question -- what the *standard requires* -- which is not this one./

Two =gpkg_data_column_constraints= rows of =constraint_type = 'range'=, which
both have =value= NULL by definition -- =value= is for =enum= and =glob=.

*Pins:* an assumption a carrying implementation will otherwise make.
=CONSTRAINT gdcc_ntv UNIQUE (constraint_name, constraint_type, value)= **does
not make range rows unique**, because SQLite treats NULLs as distinct under
UNIQUE. /Measured 2026-08-23, by accident:/ an
=INSERT INTO ... SELECT * FROM ... LIMIT 1= against a real file duplicated a
=price_range= row and the UNIQUE index accepted it. Anything that dedupes on
that key, or assumes the index makes a set, is wrong.

***And the same day, deliberately: this is not one table's peculiarity.***
Three of the four =UNIQUE= keys on the mergeable registry tables have a
nullable member -- =ge_tce= (=table_name= *and* =column_name=), =gdcc_ntv=
(=value=), =gdc_tn= (=name=) -- and only =pk_gdc= makes a set. **=ge_tce= is
the one that matters**, because every *table-scoped* extension registration has
=column_name= NULL, so it fails on files nobody had to construct: merging two
plain =ogr2ogr= outputs deduped nothing, 3 + 3 -> 6, =integrity_check= =ok=.
/That half needs no fixture -- any two =ogr2ogr= files exhibit it -- which is
why this one is still worth building: the =range= half is the case a real tool
will not hand you./

*A refinement worth keeping, or the fixture will be built wrong:* the trap is
=constraint_type = 'range'= specifically. A neighbouring
=_<domain>_domain_description= row that GDAL writes has =value= = the empty
*string*, not NULL, and dedupes correctly. Build the fixture with a real NULL,
not =''=.

** =sqlite_pagesize.gpkg= and =sqlite_reserved.gpkg=
The last two =sqlite.rs= gaps, neither of which any fixture reaches: a page
size other than 4096 (the writer hardcodes =WRITE_PAGE_SIZE=), and non-zero
reserved per-page space (the reader computes =usable_size= from header byte 20;
the writer always assumes zero).

*Build:* =PRAGMA page_size = 8192= before creating any table, and a
=PRAGMA reserved_bytes=-equivalent build for the second (SQLite exposes this
only via a VFS or =sqlite3_file_control=; failing that, patch header byte 20 by
hand and re-checksum nothing -- SQLite has no page checksums by default).

*Pins:* that a same-format run is *content*-preserving rather than
byte-preserving, which is currently a claim in the plan with nothing behind it.

* WHAT IS ALREADY COVERED, SO NOBODY REBUILDS IT
- =WITHOUT ROWID= -- =sqlite_altered.gpkg=. /Its rows were *counted* rather
  than reported as uncountable from 2026-08-23, and since 2026-08-26 the table
  is **carried**: it is the only member of this storage shape in the tree, so it
  also pins =carry::Storage::Records= and the rule that the shape follows the
  **DDL** rather than a failed table walk./
- =ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN= short records with a =DEFAULT= -- same fixture.
- =UNIQUE=, =TEXT PRIMARY KEY=, an explicit =CREATE INDEX=, and a
  =UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE= -- =sqlite_constraints.gpkg=.
- A =data_type='attributes'= registration and a minimal tile registration --
  =sqlite_contents.gpkg=. /Since 2026-08-25 it covers *carrying* the aspatial
  dataset too, not only reporting it: the two =gpkg_ogr_contents= maintenance
  triggers =ogr2ogr= attaches, a rowid gap at =9=, and both a =table=- and a
  =row=-scoped =gpkg_metadata_reference= naming it./
- Index cells past the on-page ceiling, so overflow chains -- *not a fixture*
  but =sqlite::tests::an_index_btree_survives_a_write_at_every_depth= and the
  =#[ignore]=d =sqlite_itself_validates_the_index_this_writer_builds=, both of
  which build their records in-test. /Added 2026-08-23, after the first version
  of both used uniformly short keys and never reached =write_overflow= at
  all -- the "unadventurous values" blind spot, for the third time./
